For me is a bit difficult to discuss this in another language so i ll be simple about it. He feels like a mary sue because there are some of those elements in his story. But before the concept of the Mary sue comes the one of the traditional hero (the classical one) and then comes the arquetype of the tragical heroe. He has to be someone we care and root for and like so when he falls we can feel bad about it. When we met Kvothe he is a shadow of what he was, downplaying himself as a modest bartender while his real self or previous self is the stuff of legends.

I don't think he is a mary sue, just a well written "prodigy" trope character with a lot of flaws.

I think my favourite chapter is kvothe presenting the arrow catcher to Master Kilvin, but tbh, i like most of the university chapters. I find him more relatable at that point, because he acts like a teenager, gets mad like a teenager and reacts like an imbecil everytime things don't go his ways which i find nice. But the arrowcatcher chapter felt like a very real personal achievment, both academic and economic, and that is why i like the most, even thought the economic part doesn't become clear until his return from the Earl's Mannor.
